  Council Minutes  5  02/04/2019
   Councilmember Hampton stated that his constituents are in favor
  of discontinuing the Underground Utility Districts Program; and
  spoke in favor of Councilmember McAustin's direction to continue
  the Underground Utility Districts Program, but to pause the
  collection of the Underground Surtax until the balance is spent
  down.

  The Mayor provided a PowerPoint presentation on the reasons
  why the Undergrounding District Program should be terminated
  immediately (except the Hill and Alpine model), noting that the
  project  is tremendously  complex,  provides  marginal
  improvements in terms of system reliability, will take hundreds of
  years to complete at the current pace, and is extraordinarily
  expensive. He spoke in favor of terminating the Underground
  Utility Districts Program immediately, maintain the Underground
  Surtax Fund, and suspend it until the fund balance is reduced to
  $10,000,000, and spend the funds on other eligible activities.

  Michelle White, Pasadena resident, inquired if there is an
  equitable amount of undergrounding work completed in the
  City, expressed concerns that Northwest Pasadena will be
  left out due to the economic, dense and ethnic levels.

  Councilmember Wilson stated his lack of support for the
  Underground Utility Districts Program, including the costs
  associated with the program, however, stated that many of his
  constituents are supportive of the program.

  Councilmember Masuda stated that many his constituents are not
  supportive of the Underground Utility Districts Program, and are
  requesting a refund from the Undergrou~d Surtax as a result of
  the extended period of time it will take to benefit from the program,
  and likely that it will not occur in their neighborhood.

  Vice Mayor Kennedy expressed concerns with the
  miscommunication to the City's rate payers, that some areas in
  the City would not be undergrounded; and stated that many of his
  constituents are in favor of the Underground Utility Districts
  Program, therefore he will vote in favor of continuing the program.
  He also expressed concerns with the City's ability to fairly rebate
  the Underground Surtax funds.
